newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Cricket-Tendulkar, Azharuddin share record stand.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Tendulkar, Azharuddin share record stand.

text.p: A record sixth wicket partnership by any country against South Africa steered India towards safety on the third day of the second test on Saturday.
Captain Sachin Tendulkar and Mohammad Azharuddin both scored centuries in a stand of 222 that lifted India from 58 for five to 293 for six at tea.
It exceeded the previous highest sixth wicket partnership against South Africa of 206 by England's Ken Barrigton and Jim Parks at Durban in the 1964-65 series.
Azharuddin scored 115 and Tendulkar was unbeaten on 125 at the interval with his team 37 short of their target of 330 to avoid the follow-on.
Both batsmen were uncharacteristically dropped by the South Africans in the afternoon session -- Tendulkar on 80 and Azharuddin on 55 and 68 -- as they went on a thunderous attack.

They added 100 in the first hour after lunch with Azharuddin reaching his third century in four tests against South Africa in only 96 balls, hitting 16 fours and one six on the way. In all he batted five minutes short of three hours and hit 20 boundaries in his 109-ball 115.
Tendulkar beat him to three figures with a hardly less explosive innings, reaching his century in 138 balls with 16 fours.
They were finally separated when Azharuddin was sent back attempting an impossible single to be run out by Andrew Hudson's throw from backward point.
They had come together after India had slumped from their overnight 29 for three to 58 for five in the first eight overs of the day.
Allan Donald had Saurav Ganguly caught in the slips for 23 to the third ball of the day and V.V.S. Laxman made five before gloving Shaun Pollock to wicketkeeper Dave Richardson down the legside.
India must avoid defeat to keep alive the series after they lost the first of the three tests by 328 runs in Durban.
